title: Slim prefetch & session-checkpoint affinity rewrite
creator: Alex Chen
description: Refactor the prefetch token allocator and session checkpoint affinity to reduce contention and memory churn in the continuous batching path. Objective is to remove a global lock hotspot during KV snapshot/rehydration, introduce locality for prefetch allocation, and make scheduler handoffs between enqueue and prefetch threads lock-avoidant. This will simplify the checkpoints lifecycle and improve p95/p99 tail stability under mixed short/long sequence workloads.
acceptance_criteria: Reduce p99 token generation latency (host-side) by >= 30% on synthetic mixed workload compared to baseline v2.3
Decrease global KV snapshot stall occurrences during 99th-percentile bursts by at least 80% in the stress harness
No increase in token-level unit cost beyond 5% for steady-state throughput; memory usage at steady-state remains within +10% of baseline
Automated unit/integration tests covering checkpoint epoch transitions and prefetch reclaim paths merged
Canary rollout shows no customer-facing errors for 48 hours at 1% traffic and metrics meet SLOs; ability to rollback via feature flag within 5 minutes
design_decisions: Move from a single global prefetch allocator to per-worker (per-core) prefetch buckets to reduce cross-thread contention
Checkpoint store rewritten as append-only segment files with lightweight epoch references instead of full copy-on-write snapshots
Scheduler handoff will be implemented via lock-free single-writer queues plus a small bounded cooperative handback buffer to preserve fairness
KV rehydrate will use lazy shallow-refs and a background compaction worker to avoid blocking hot request paths
Introduce a runtime-configurable 'prefetch-window' and 'checkpoint-epoch' feature flags for gradual rollout and experimentation
implementation_notes: Phase 1: Add per-worker prefetch buckets and metrics. Keep global allocator as fallback. (branch: feat/prefetch-buckets)
Phase 2: Implement append-only checkpoint segment store and epoch refs. Expose metrics for segment growth and compaction latency.
Phase 3: Replace handoff path with lock-free SPSC queues and cooperative buffer. Add instrumentation for failed handoffs and backpressure events.
Phase 4: Integrate with canary toggles, add automated migration tests that simulate mid-request epoch flips and KV rehydrate interruptions.
Keep compatibility shim for existing KV index layout for one release cycle to support rollback.
testing_plan: Unit tests for prefetch bucket allocation, reclaim, and corner cases (empty/refill)
Integration tests that simulate checkpoint epoch boundary during inflight requests
Load harness: mixed short (<=64 tokens) and long (>=2048 tokens) sequence workloads with 0-30% concurrency spikes
Chaos test: random prefetch worker crashes and stash/rehydrate to validate recovery and zero-data-loss invariant
Performance benchmarks comparing memory, CPU, and p95/p99 latency vs runtime-2.3 baseline on same infra
rollout_plan: Merge behind feature flags: prefetch_buckets_enabled and epoch_checkpoint_enabled
Internal canary at 0.1% traffic for 4 hours, validate metrics and logs
External canary at 1% traffic for 48 hours; monitor 'batcher_handoff_failures', 'kv_snapshot_stall', 'token_latency_p99'
Gradual ramp to 10% then 50% over subsequent days if metrics are healthy
If regressions detected, flip feature flag and retain logs for postmortem
risks_mitigation: Risk: subtle correctness bug on epoch transitions. Mitigation: exhaustive migration tests + property-based test for rehydrate semantics
Risk: increased memory due to append-only segments. Mitigation: aggressive compaction policy and metrics alerting for segment growth
Risk: rollback complexity. Mitigation: maintain compatibility shim and ensure fast-path is behind feature flag
Risk: unexpected scheduler fairness regressions. Mitigation: perf tests with synthetic adversarial request patterns and a fallback to cooperative buffer size tuning
